observed_anchors.observation: Host intrinsic arity/effect class can be observed, but every current host intrinsic is rejected with HOST_INTRINSIC_TYPE_SIGNATURE_UNBOUND because explicit Clay parameter/return types are absent.
Executable TypedIR v1 admits only CLAY_FN calls; non-Clay calls, including INTRINSIC, fail closed. materialize_source currently analyzes with an empty host-contract map.

The single VM already contains OP_HOSTCALL and a capability-gated backend call id 1 bound to capability linux.uname_hash, but the current source-level HOST_CONTRACTS registry has no linux.uname_hash entry. Hostcall arguments/results are integer-only.
Canonical ClayOS launch is provenance-strict and executes the single ClayVM, but it does not expose real Linux subprocess/process-tree semantics.

Current CM-08 is OPEN; CM-TERM explicitly lacks canonical Clay argv/env/cwd/stdin/stdout/stderr/PTY effects. Current workspace also selects canonical Bytes/Buffer ownership+lifetime as the highest-value shared I/O prerequisite.

generated_reality.hypothesis: Adding a Linux subprocess runner directly beneath ClayOS is premature. The causal predecessor is one canonical typed host ABI shared by analyzer, nominal checker, executable TypedIR, single-VM lowering and capability dispatch; process I/O must then reuse the canonical Bytes/Buffer value model rather than invent a process-only representation.
generated_reality.mechanism: A typed intrinsic contract must bind source call identity, parameter/return Clay types, effect class, capability identity and stable VM hostcall identity before executable IR admission. The process family then binds argv/cwd/env/stdin/stdout/stderr/exit/timeout to typed values and executes only through the same single VM/ClayOS path.
generated_reality.strongest_counter_reality: Use integer handles or a direct host-side subprocess facade now and add type/value semantics later.
generated_reality.counter_reality_disposition: DEFER. It can produce an early demo but would put process meaning in an out-of-band host table/direct facade, violating the current no-hidden-second-semantics and VM/direct/executable-equivalence laws unless the handle/value contract itself is first canonicalized.

unusual_experiment.name: CM_PROC_TIMEOUT_DESCENDANT_ESCAPE
unusual_experiment.baseline: A Python parent spawned /bin/sleep 20 as a descendant. Timeout cleanup killed only the direct child.
unusual_experiment.intervention: Launch the process in a new session/process group and kill the whole group on timeout.
unusual_experiment.rollback: All disposable descendant processes were killed; observed Z means terminated/not running, not a claim of immediate parent reaping.
unusual_experiment.interpretation: A CM-PROC timeout contract that only terminates the direct child is insufficient for process-tree cleanup. The eventual Linux adapter must define process-group/session ownership and bounded cleanup/reaping semantics.

primary_mechanism_evidence: Python subprocess documentation: run/Popen expose argv, cwd, env, stdio and timeout behavior; timeout handling of the direct child does not by itself define descendant cleanup.
Linux kill(2): negative pid targets a process group.
Linux setsid(2): a new session creates a distinct process group/session boundary usable for scoped cleanup.
